tldr: Headlines globally reduce the story to a single legal act — a court ordering SK Group's chairman to pay his ex-wife $640–644 million — with the record-scale dollar amount the only secondary signal visible at title level. The slush-fund political backstory, AI-sector asset rationale, and spousal-contribution equity argument that dominate body coverage are entirely absent from titles.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only headline to anonymise the subject as 'Tech titan' rather than naming SK Group or Chairman Chey — positioning this as a celebrity wealth story rather than a corporate-governance or legal event.

Only headline framed from the ex-wife's perspective ('Ex-wife of SK chief wins'), inverting the payer-subject framing universal elsewhere and foregrounding the ruling as her judicial victory rather than his court penalty.
Only headline to embed the cultural label 'divorce of the century' directly in the title, surfacing the national-media spectacle framing that every other outlet confined to body text.

bottom_line: Headline coverage strips the story to its legal core — a court ordering the SK chairman to pay his ex-wife — with financial scale the only embellishment visible in titles, while the political dynasty context, AI-sector valuation rationale, and gender-equity subtext that run through body coverage remain entirely invisible above the fold.
